- [USER] User expressed interest in the science behind aromatherapy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Aromatherapy involves the use of essential oils extracted from plants to improve physical and mental well-being.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The fragrant molecules from essential oils are inhaled and can affect the body and mind.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The olfactory system is responsible for our sense of smell, and inhaling essential oils affects the brain's limbic system, which regulates emotions, motivation, and memory.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Research shows that lavender and peppermint can have a calming effect, while lemon and rosemary can improve alertness and cognitive function.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Essential oils can be diluted and applied topically, but some can be toxic if used improperly.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is recommended to consult with a qualified aromatherapist or healthcare provider before using essential oils.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Other commonly used essential oils include peppermint, eucalyptus, lemon, and tea tree.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Peppermint is used to boost energy and improve concentration; eucalyptus is known for respiratory benefits; lemon promotes cheerfulness; tea tree has antiseptic properties.
